text:
Priya: Quick post-all-hands follow-up — started this thread for the questions we ran out of time on about release cadence, oncall, quality bars, and SLAs. I'll collect short answers and action items here.

Marta: Thanks — first: can you confirm the cadence? are we weekly, biweekly, monthly for prod releases? and how do we treat hotfixes?

Jasper: Short answer: split cadence. Minor/patch releases: weekly train. Major releases (breaking or feature bundles): monthly. Hotfixes go through oncall patch flow and can ship immediately after CA/triage.

Jasper: Example rollout policy we'll use by default:
```
rollout:
  canary: 5%
  monitor: 10m
  promote: 30%
  full: 24h
```

Leo: To be explicit about rollback/alerts: canary failures -> auto-rollback after 3 failed health checks; pager to oncall + eng-owner if >5% error rate sustained for 5m.

Marta: Cool. Next: quality gate — do we require full e2e for every PR? That was a concern from product.

Leo: No, not for every PR. Required checks: unit tests + integration tests + lint + basic smoke. Full e2e runs on the release candidate pipeline and for features flagged GA. If a change touches infra or routing, e2e is mandatory before staging promote.

Anita: For Sales/Support—what are the SLA commitments we announced for Dedicated customers? I need exact numbers to communicate.

Jasper: Dedicated SLA summary: uptime 99.95% (monthly), p99 latency SLO depends on model family; baseline p99 target for small models is 250ms, for large models it's 800ms. Pricing/commit tiers determine stricter targets. We'll publish a clear matrix in /docs/sla next week.

Anita: Thanks — is there a formal escalation path for SLA breaches?

Leo: Yes — escalation: support -> eng oncall -> account eng -> infra oncall -> exec oncall if unresolved after 4 hours. We'll add runbook links to the SLA doc.

Priya: Action items: 1) Jasper to drop the SLA matrix + doc link by Tue. 2) Leo to add rollout + rollback snippets to the release playbook. 3) Marta to update PR checklist w/ e2e rules. I'll create a follow-up calendar invite for a 30m release-process sync.

Jasper: +1 on that. Also want to emphasize: teams should rely on automated canary metrics we built into the console — per-route error, latency spikes, token-rate anomalies. If you want access to the advanced dashboards for your service, ping me or @Leo.

DeployBot: Release train 2026.03.15-weekly deployed to canary (5%) — monitoring hooks active :rocket:

Marta: One more quick Q — will we keep the weekly train time fixed? it used to jump around and caused conflicts with demos.

Jasper: We'll lock the train to Tuesdays 02:00 UTC for now. If that causes conflicts we'll iterate.

Priya: Thanks everyone. If you have follow-ups, reply here. I'll close this thread after I post the doc and calendar invite. :white_check_mark:
